Subject: Discovery recap: Finly p95 latency & concurrency requirements

Tom / Priya — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap + next steps so we have alignment before the SRE deep-dive.

Summary of pain & goals
- Pain: Your current streaming customer-facing endpoint is experiencing p95 tail latency spikes (~600–800ms) which makes the live chat/assist UX feel sluggish and causes session drop-offs.
- Goal: Deliver an interactive streaming experience with p95 <= 200ms for first-byte/partial tokens and an end-to-end p95 that feels <300ms for typical prompts.
- Concurrency: Target sustained concurrency ~200 streams with burst capacity up to 400 during peak events.
- Success criteria: p95 steady-state under 200ms (first-byte), under 300ms end-to-end for 95% of requests during a 1-hour peak window; error rate <0.5%; model quality parity to current baseline.

Current stack (what you told us)
- Custom LLM infra running on mixed GPU fleet (A100 + T4/GPU autoscale), inference through an in-house k8s/Triton pipeline.
- Prefix caching in some paths, but KV cache and batching are not yet tuned for streaming.
- Simple rate-based autoscaler; no model-variant fallbacks currently.

Key constraints / gotchas
- Streaming UX depends heavily on first-byte latency (partial tokens) more than token throughput.
- You need predictable SLOs during promotional spikes (quarterly product launches).
- Security/compliance: data-in-motion must remain within your VPC for the POC.

Proposed next steps (what Redwood will do + asks for Finly)
1) SRE deep-dive (60–90m) to collect traces, traffic shape, and a small load profile. Can we lock a time next week? Suggested: Thu 2026-09-24 or Fri 2026-09-25 morning PT.
2) Share traces + load profile (we requested the perf traces during the call). Please drop the perf traces and traffic spreadsheet to the Drive link or reply here.
3) Redwood will propose a mutual action plan (MAP) with a 2-week POC scope (Dedicated/Private options), test harness, and success metrics. Draft MAP attached (finly_map_v1.xlsx + redwood_map_mvp.pdf).
4) Sales/Procurement: I'll loop in our contracts lead once the POC scope looks good.

If I've misstated anything please correct. Would love confirmation on the p95/concurrency numbers as we scope.

Thanks — talk soon.

—

Marissa — thanks for the concise recap, this is great. A few clarifications from our side:

- Current numbers: p95 observed for streaming first-byte is ~700–800ms on average during business hours; end-to-end p95 ~1.1s for longer prompts.
- Target: We'd like to aim for p95 first-byte <= 150–200ms and end-to-end p95 <= 300ms for the majority of our internal beta users. Reducing jitter is as important as lowering median.
- Concurrency: 200 sustained is accurate; we need burst headroom to ~400 for peak campaigns.
- Model / infra specifics: We run a tuned LLM (proprietary checkpoints, roughly similar throughput to gpt-3.5 on equivalent hardware) on a mix of A100 and T4 instances behind a k8s-based autoscaler. Triton in front, custom batching layer.
- What we can share now: I've uploaded a sampled set of server-side traces + a 48h traffic profile to the shared Drive, and attached a zip of traces to this thread. Should help your SREs reproduce the tail.

On timing — Thu 9/24 10:00–11:30 PT works for our infra lead (Priya) and me. If that's good, let's lock it.

Thanks,
Tom
